advances: A determinant and contact theorem for an already maximizing full-continuous-dimension extraction. General objective-one stress is obtained only under the stated qualifications.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Take the positive-fiber hull $E=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times D_z)$. Apply the positive-volume case of 69166b0fcb73425a to $Q=D$ with the full base plane and lattice $\mathbb Z^n$. Its hypotheses hold because $D$ is compact convex and has positive mixed $d$-volume. It gives the exact original fibers over $P$ and no other integer fibers of $E$. Since the projection of $E$ is $\operatorname{conv}P$, it also gives the stated completeness of $P$.

The affine bijection $F(z,x)=(z,Tx+Bz+b)$ sends $E$ to the hull of the fitted fibers, contained in $C$ because the fitted generators are. Its integer fibers are exactly those fitted fibers, since $F$ leaves bases fixed. If $\operatorname{aff}P=\mathbb R^n$, this hull is already full dimensional, using one full $d$-fiber and the $n$ independent base directions. Otherwise put $L=\operatorname{aff}P$. Fix a hyperplane containing $L$ and a positive distance $\eta$ at most the distance of every integer base of $C$ outside $L$ to $L$. Such an $\eta$ exists by finiteness, with any positive choice if there are no such bases. Choose a small closed ambient ball in $\operatorname{int}C$ whose projection lies strictly on one side of that hyperplane and at distance less than $\eta$ from $L$. To obtain it, approach a point of $F(E)$ by interior points of $C$ and take a nearby interior point off the hyperplane, which exists because the interior is open. Shrink a ball there to satisfy both strict conditions. The convex hull with this ball stays inside $C$ and is full dimensional. The convexity of distance to $L$ excludes all integer bases of $C$ outside $L$. Over $L$ a positive coefficient on any point from the ball is impossible by the one-sided hyperplane, so the trace over $L$ is unchanged. This is the exact one-sided thickening from 5827666c5ec237a1 with the ball chosen inside $C$.

The resulting measure is $\det(T)$ times the pushforward of the original mixed measure under $F$. The original null fibers contribute zero. The centroid therefore transforms by $F$, and normalized depth is unchanged because $F$ bijects the containing closed halfspaces. The transformed centroid has the same integer base, so maximality yields $\det T\le1$.

Work in affine coordinates of $\operatorname{aff}P$ for the base argument of the shear, using $k$ centered coordinates $z'$. Affine functions there extend to the original base space. At identity write the parameters as $(A,B,b)=(T-I_d,B,b)$ in these coordinates. The fitting constraints are linear inequalities
$$
u\cdot(Ax+Bz'+b)\le h_{C_z}(u)-u\cdot x
\quad(z\in P,\ x\in D_z,\ \lVert u\rVert_2=1).
$$
The indexed family is compact with nonnegative continuous slack. The gradient of a constraint in the product Euclidean parameter pairing is $G=(ux^\top,uz'^\top,u)$, and the determinant gradient at identity is $g=(I_d,0,0)$. The active constraints are precisely the stated contacts.

If a direction $v$ has $g\cdot v>0$ and $G\cdot v<0$ at every contact, it gives a feasible small positive step. Indeed, the compact set of constraints with $G\cdot v\ge0$ has positive minimum slack when nonempty, and the pairings are bounded. Constraints with negative pairing already remain feasible. The determinant is positive and increases on a sufficiently short step, contradicting maximality. If zero were outside the compact convex hull of the active gradients and $-g$, strict separation would produce exactly such a direction. A convex combination for zero and Carathéodory's theorem in dimension $p$ yield $\sum_i\lambda_iG_i=\alpha g$ with at most $p+1$ contact terms and coefficients as stated. The weights on the contacts cannot all vanish because $g\ne0$. When $\alpha>0$, divide by it and apply conic Carathéodory to use at most $p$ contacts.

The reduced base balance and translation balance imply the original base balance by writing $z$ as an affine function of $z'$. Expanding any $q(z_i)$ in these equations gives the affine cancellation. Taking the trace of the first equation and using the contact identities gives the supporting-value sum.

A strict fit pairs strictly negatively with every active gradient when taken as a direction from identity. Pairing with any pure abnormal combination would give a strictly negative sum equal to zero. Hence the alternative then has $\alpha>0$. A graph inside all target interiors is already such a fit with $T_0=0$.

For polytopes, impose the finite system of every source vertex against every target facet. The cone of active gradients is closed: conic Carathéodory with elimination of linearly dependent generators expresses it as a finite union of cones on linearly independent subsets, each closed in its span and in the parameter space. If $g$ were outside this cone, separation would give a direction $v$ with $g\cdot v>0$ and $G\cdot v\le0$ on all active pairs. Finitely many strictly slack constraints permit a sufficiently small positive step, again contradicting determinant maximality. Thus $g$ is in the active cone, and conic Carathéodory yields at most $p$ active pairs. Unit-normal normalization only rescales their positive coefficients.

statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be an ambient compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and let $D\subseteq C$ be an ambient convex body maximizing positive mixed $d$-volume among those whose true centroid $(j,c)$ has integral $j$ and whose normalized closed-halfspace depth at that centroid is at least a prescribed $\beta$. Write $\mu$ for mixed $d$-volume, $P=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:|D_z|_d>0\}$, $k=\dim\operatorname{aff}P$, and $p=d^2+dk+d$.

The set $P$ equals $\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Every affine fit
$$
T D_z+Bz+b\subseteq C_z\quad(z\in P),\qquad \det T>0
$$
is realizable by an ambient convex body inside $C$ with exactly the transformed positive integer fibers, mass $\det(T)\mu(D)$, true centroid $(j,Tc+Bj+b)$ and the same normalized depth there. In particular every such fit has $\det T\le1$.

There are at most $p+1$ contacts $(z_i,x_i,u_i)$ with $z_i\in P$, $x_i\in D_{z_i}$, $\lVert u_i\rVert_2=1$, and $u_i\cdot x_i=h_{C_{z_i}}(u_i)$, with nonnegative weights $\lambda_i$ and $\alpha\ge0$, $\alpha+\sum_i\lambda_i>0$, such that
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i x_i^\top=\alpha I_d,qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i z_i^\top=0,qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0 .
$$
If $\alpha>0$ the stress can be normalized to $\alpha=1$ with at most $p$ contacts. For every affine $q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d$ the equations give $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i(x_i-q(z_i))^\top=\alpha I_d$, and $\sum_i\lambda_i h_{C_{z_i}}(u_i)=\alpha d$.

A normalized stress exists if either there is an affine fit $T_0D_z+B_0z+b_0\subset\operatorname{int}(C_z)$ for all $z\in P$, with arbitrary $T_0$, or all the $D_z,C_z$ for $z\in P$ are polytopes. An affine graph taking values in $\operatorname{int}(C_z)$ at every $z\in P$ suffices for the strict fit.
title: Integer-fiber determinant maximality and finite contact certificates
